events.description: American stock market crash triggered global Great Depression, France also impacted, though slightly later than other countries. Unemployment rose, industrial production declined, social unrest intensified. Economic crisis intensified political polarization, far-right (fascist) and far-left (communist) forces grew. Centrist governments powerless to address crisis, frequently changed. Great Depression weakened democratic institutions, paving way for 1930s political crisis and ultimate defeat.

events.title: February 6 Crisis
events.description: Far-right groups demonstrated in Paris, attempted to storm parliament, protesting government corruption (Stavisky scandal). Demonstration evolved into violent clashes, 15 dead, thousands injured. Event viewed as fascist coup attempt, shocking republicans. To counter far-right threat, left-wing parties (Socialist, Communist, Radical) formed Popular Front alliance. February 6 crisis marked French politics' radicalization, left-right opposition intensified, democratic institutions threatened.

events.title: Popular Front Government
events.description: Popular Front won 1936 election, Socialist leader Léon Blum became France's first Jewish prime minister. Government implemented major social reforms: 40-hour work week, paid vacation, collective bargaining rights. These reforms improved workers' lives, but also caused strong opposition from capitalists and right-wing, slogan 'Better Hitler than Blum.' Economic difficulties and Spanish Civil War divided Popular Front, 1938 government collapsed. Popular Front's legacy contradictory: social progress but economic problems, unity but ultimate division.

events.title: Munich Agreement
events.description: French Prime Minister Daladier and British Prime Minister Chamberlain met with Hitler and Mussolini in Munich, agreed to cede Czechoslovakia's Sudetenland to Germany in exchange for 'peace for our time.' France betrayed ally Czechoslovakia, hoping to avoid war through appeasement. Daladier cheered upon returning to Paris, but he said 'Ah, the fools.' Munich Agreement was appeasement policy's pinnacle, but failed to stop Hitler, instead encouraged his aggression. Agreement became symbol of shame, 'Munich' became synonym for weak surrender.

events.title: Declaration of War on Germany
events.description: After Germany invaded Poland, France and Britain declared war on Germany, World War II began. France mobilized army, but adopted defensive strategy, relying on Maginot Line. Winter 1939-1940 was 'Phoney War,' almost no fighting on Western Front. French army morale low, leadership conservative, strategy outdated. France failed to help Poland, also failed to attack while Germany fighting on Eastern Front. Phoney War's passivity foreshadowed 1940's disastrous defeat.

events.title: Battle of France and Fall
events.description: Germany launched Blitzkrieg, bypassed Maginot Line, invaded France through Ardennes Forest. German forces rapidly broke through, surrounded Allied forces, British evacuated at Dunkirk. French army collapsed, government fled Paris. June 14, Germans entered Paris without fight. June 22, Marshal Pétain signed armistice at Compiègne (where Germany surrendered 1918), France surrendered. France divided into German-occupied zone and Vichy free zone. Battle of France lasted only six weeks, France's most painful defeat in history, shocking world. Powerful French army rapidly collapsed, exposing military and political failures.

events.title: Vichy France
events.description: Marshal Pétain established government at Vichy, collaborating with Germany. Vichy regime abolished republic, established authoritarian 'French State,' motto 'Work, Family, Fatherland.' Vichy collaborated with Nazis, persecuted Jews, sent workers to Germany, suppressed Resistance. Laval and others actively promoted collaboration. But Vichy also claimed to protect France from worse fate. Vichy period was France's darkest period, moral dilemmas of collaboration vs resistance, survival vs honor tore society apart. After war, Vichy legacy became taboo, not confronted until 1970s.

events.title: De Gaulle's London Appeal
events.description: Exiled General de Gaulle in London broadcast speech via BBC, calling on French to continue resistance, refusing to accept defeat. He said 'France has lost a battle, but France has not lost the war.' De Gaulle established Free French movement, organized government-in-exile and army. June 18 speech became symbol of French resistance, de Gaulle became resistance leader. But few heard speech at time, de Gaulle sentenced to death by Vichy government. De Gaulle's persistence and vision ultimately vindicated, he became postwar France's savior and leader.

events.title: French Resistance
events.description: French people launched Resistance movement against German occupation and Vichy collaboration. Resisters included Communists, Gaullists, Socialists, Christians and various factions. They conducted sabotage, intelligence, assassination, helped Allied airmen escape. Jean Moulin unified Resistance, established National Council of Resistance. Resisters risked lives, many arrested, tortured, executed or sent to concentration camps. Resistance played important role after D-Day, liberating Paris and other cities. Resistance became symbol of French honor, mythologized after war, but actually only minority participated, most chose compliance or observation.

events.title: Vel' d'Hiv Roundup
events.description: Vichy police in Paris rounded up 13,000 Jews including 4,000 children, detained at Vélodrome d'Hiver stadium in terrible conditions. Subsequently they sent to Drancy internment camp, ultimately deported to Auschwitz extermination camp, almost none survived. Vel' d'Hiv Roundup was most notorious example of Vichy collaboration in persecuting Jews. French police not Germans executed roundup, showing Vichy's active collaboration. This event long covered up, not until 1995 President Chirac acknowledged France's responsibility, saying 'That day, France committed unforgivable crime.'

events.title: D-Day Normandy Landings
events.description: Allied forces launched D-Day landings on Normandy beaches, opening second front, beginning liberation of Western Europe. French Resistance coordinated with landings, sabotaging German communications and transport. Fighting fierce, Allies paid heavy price, but successfully established beachhead. Normandy landings was WWII's turning point, marking beginning of Germany's defeat on Western Front. French people welcomed liberators, but Normandy campaign also caused massive French civilian casualties and city destruction. Landings paved way for France's liberation.

events.title: Liberation of Paris
events.description: Allied forces and French 2nd Armored Division under General Leclerc liberated Paris. Paris Resistance rose up, erected barricades, fought German forces. German commander Choltitz disobeyed Hitler's order to destroy Paris, surrendered to Leclerc. August 26, de Gaulle triumphantly entered Paris, paraded down Champs-Élysées, cheered by hundreds of thousands. Paris liberation was one of most exciting moments in French history, symbolizing restoration of freedom and honor. But liberation also accompanied by revenge against collaborators, thousands executed or humiliated.

events.title: Provisional Government and Reconstruction
events.description: De Gaulle led provisional government, restored republic, purged collaborators, rebuilt nation. Women gained suffrage, social security system established, major industries nationalized. De Gaulle insisted on France's status as victor, gained UN Security Council permanent seat and German occupation zone. But de Gaulle clashed with parties, resigned 1946. Constituent assembly drafted new constitution, establishing Fourth Republic. Postwar France faced enormous challenges: economic reconstruction, colonial crisis, Cold War, but also experienced 'Trente Glorieuses' prosperity.

events.title: Fourth Republic
events.description: Fourth Republic established parliamentary system, but government extremely unstable, over 20 governments in 12 years. Parties divided, coalitions fragile, prime ministers frequently changed. Despite political chaos, French economy grew rapidly, modernization accelerated, participated in European integration (Coal and Steel Community, European Economic Community). But Fourth Republic couldn't resolve colonial crises, especially Indochina and Algerian wars. 1958, Algerian crisis led to Fourth Republic's collapse, de Gaulle returned to power, establishing Fifth Republic.

events.title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu and Indochina Withdrawal
events.description: French forces besieged and defeated by Viet Minh at Dien Bien Phu, France's most painful colonial defeat. France attempted to establish fortress in valley, but Viet Minh under General Vo Nguyen Giap dragged artillery up mountains, besieged French. After 56 days fighting, French surrendered, 10,000 captured. Dien Bien Phu forced France to abandon Indochina, Geneva Accords divided Vietnam into North and South. Dien Bien Phu marked beginning of French colonial empire's end, also foreshadowed America's future failure in Vietnam.

events.title: Algerian War
events.description: Algerian National Liberation Front launched independence war, France sent large army to suppress. War extremely brutal, both sides used torture and terrorism. France had million European settlers (pieds-noirs) in Algeria, viewed it as French homeland. War tore French society, army clashed with government, 1958 army mutiny led to Fourth Republic's collapse. De Gaulle regained power, ultimately decided to grant Algeria independence, angering pieds-noirs and army, Secret Army Organization (OAS) launched terrorist attacks. 1962 Évian Accords, Algeria independent, million pieds-noirs fled to France. Algerian War was one of France's most painful conflicts, trauma still unhealed.

events.title: Treaty of Rome and European Integration
events.description: France with Germany, Italy, Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg signed Treaty of Rome, establishing European Economic Community (EEC), EU's predecessor. Treaty established common market, promoted trade and economic integration. France played leadership role in European integration, forming Franco-German axis with Germany. European integration was cornerstone of postwar French diplomacy, aiming to prevent war, promote prosperity, maintain French influence. France's role in EU always central but also full of contradictions, struggling between sovereignty and integration.

events.title: Fifth Republic Established
events.description: During Algerian crisis, de Gaulle recalled to power, drafted new constitution, establishing Fifth Republic. New constitution greatly strengthened presidential powers, president directly elected (after 1962), appoints prime minister, can dissolve parliament, possesses emergency powers. Fifth Republic ended Fourth Republic's political instability, established strong executive power. De Gaulle became first president, ruled until 1969. Fifth Republic constitution still in use today, France's most stable regime in history, though also criticized as 'republican monarchy,' presidential power excessive.

events.title: French Nuclear Weapons Test
events.description: France conducted first nuclear weapons test in Algerian Sahara Desert, becoming fourth nuclear power. De Gaulle insisted on developing independent nuclear deterrent (force de frappe) to ensure France's independence and great power status, not relying on American nuclear umbrella. Nuclear weapons became core of French diplomacy and military policy, symbolizing its great power status. But nuclear tests also raised environmental and health concerns, and international criticism. France maintains nuclear arsenal to this day, one pillar of its Security Council permanent seat.

events.title: Franco-German Friendship Treaty
events.description: De Gaulle signed Élysée Treaty with German Chancellor Adenauer, formally ending Franco-German enmity, establishing friendly cooperative relations. Treaty stipulated regular consultations between two countries, promoting cultural and youth exchanges. Franco-German reconciliation was one of postwar Europe's most important achievements, laying foundation for European integration. Franco-German axis became EU's engine, close relations between leaders (de Gaulle-Adenauer, Mitterrand-Kohl, Macron-Merkel) drove European process. Franco-German Friendship Treaty symbolized transformation from war to peace, from hatred to cooperation.

events.title: Withdrawal from NATO Military Integration
events.description: De Gaulle announced France's withdrawal from NATO military integrated command, demanded American troops leave French bases, to maintain French independence. De Gaulle criticized American hegemony, pursued independent diplomacy and defense policy. France retained NATO membership, but didn't participate in military command. This decision reflected de Gaulle's nationalism and insistence on France's great power status. France didn't fully reintegrate into NATO until 2009 under Sarkozy. De Gaulle's independent policy shaped French diplomatic tradition, emphasizing sovereignty and multipolar world.

events.title: May 1968 Events
events.description: Student and worker movement swept France, challenging de Gaulle government and traditional authority. Movement began with Paris university student protests, rapidly spread, students occupied Sorbonne, erected barricades, clashed with police. Workers joined, 10 million on strike, paralyzing nation. Protesters demanded educational reform, workers' rights, social change, slogans 'It is forbidden to forbid,' 'Imagination seizes power.' De Gaulle momentarily lost control, fled to Germany, but ultimately restored order, dissolved parliament, won election. May 1968 failed to overthrow government, but profoundly changed French society, challenged patriarchy, authoritarianism and conservative values, opening cultural and social liberalization.

events.title: De Gaulle's Resignation
events.description: De Gaulle resigned after 1969 referendum defeat. Referendum concerned Senate reform and decentralization, de Gaulle viewed it as confidence vote. Referendum failed with 53% opposition, de Gaulle immediately resigned, retired to countryside. 1970, de Gaulle died, aged 79. De Gaulle was 20th century France's most important figure, led Resistance, established Fifth Republic, restored France's great power status. His legacy complex: nationalism, authoritarianism but also modernization, European integration. Gaullism became French political tradition, influencing to this day.

events.title: First Oil Crisis
events.description: Arab oil-exporting countries imposed oil embargo on West due to Yom Kippur War, triggering first oil crisis. Oil prices quadrupled within months, severely impacting French economy. Economic growth stagnated, unemployment rose, inflation intensified, opening era of 'stagflation.' Oil crisis ended thirty post-war years of economic prosperity ('Trente Glorieuses'), forcing France to reconsider energy policy. Government heavily developed nuclear power, by 1980s France became one of world's highest nuclear energy percentage countries. Oil crisis marked end of post-war economic golden age.

events.title: Giscard d'Estaing Elected President
events.description: Valéry Giscard d'Estaing elected after President Pompidou's sudden death, becoming Fifth Republic's youngest president (48 years old). Giscard represented moderate conservatism, promoted social modernization and liberal reforms. He lowered age of majority to 18, legalized abortion (Veil Law, 1975), expanded divorce rights, promoted women's rights. Economically, he faced oil crisis and stagflation, promoted European integration, established close relationship with German Chancellor Schmidt, laying foundation for European Monetary System. Giscard's rule (1974-1981) was period of modernization but also full of economic challenges.

events.title: Mitterrand Elected President
events.description: Socialist candidate François Mitterrand elected president, Fifth Republic's first left-wing victory, ending 23 years of right-wing rule. Mitterrand promised social change, appointed left-wing government including Communists. Government implemented nationalizations, increased social welfare, abolished death penalty, 39-hour work week, fifth week paid vacation. But economic difficulties forced Mitterrand to turn in 1983, adopting austerity policies. Mitterrand ruled 14 years (1981-1995), Fifth Republic's longest-serving president, promoted European integration, established major cultural projects (Louvre Pyramid, new National Library).

events.title: French Revolution Bicentennial
events.description: France grandly celebrated Revolution's 200th anniversary, holding parades, exhibitions and cultural activities. President Mitterrand presided over celebrations, inviting world leaders to participate. Celebrations reassessed revolutionary legacy, affirming human rights and democratic ideals, also reflecting on Reign of Terror and violence. Bicentennial coincided with Berlin Wall fall and Eastern European communism collapse, revolutionary ideals' victory seemed vindicated. Celebrations reinforced France's self-image as birthplace of human rights and freedom, but also triggered debates about revolutionary violence and legacy.

events.title: Maastricht Treaty
events.description: France ratified Maastricht Treaty, establishing European Union, introducing euro. Referendum passed by narrow 51% majority, showing France's division over European integration. Mitterrand and Chirac supported treaty, but both left and right had opponents, fearing sovereignty loss. Maastricht marked deepening of European integration, from economic community to political union. France's role in EU continued central but contradictory, struggling between promoting integration and protecting sovereignty. European question became dividing line in French politics, remains so today.

events.title: Chirac Acknowledges Vichy Responsibility
events.description: President Jacques Chirac delivered speech at Vel' d'Hiv Roundup commemoration, first time officially acknowledging France's (not just Vichy regime's) responsibility in Holocaust. Chirac said 'That day, France committed unforgivable crime...France, home of all French, betrayed her promise.' This broke postwar silence and denial, acknowledging French police and officials' collaboration in persecuting Jews. Chirac's speech was important moment of confronting history, promoting reflection and memory work on Vichy period, though also causing controversy.

events.title: Euro Circulation
events.description: France and other eurozone countries began using euro banknotes and coins, replacing franc. Franc used for centuries, symbol of French identity, its disappearance caused nostalgia and concern. But euro transition relatively smooth, becoming tangible symbol of European integration. Euro facilitated trade and travel, but also limited monetary policy autonomy. Euro crisis (2010s) exposed single currency problems, triggering euro questioning. But euro remains EU's core achievement, France its major supporter.

events.title: EU Constitution Referendum Defeat
events.description: France rejected EU Constitutional Treaty in referendum with 55% opposition, shocking Europe. Left opposed neoliberalism, right opposed sovereignty loss, populace worried about globalization and eastward expansion. President Chirac and mainstream parties supported constitution, but defeat showed elite-populace disconnect. Referendum defeat was major setback for European integration, constitution abandoned, later passed as Lisbon Treaty (without referendum). 2005 referendum reflected France's anxieties about Europe, globalization and identity, foreshadowing populism's rise.

events.title: Charlie Hebdo Attack
events.description: Islamic extremists attacked satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo's Paris office, killing 12 including cartoonists and editors, revenge for magazine publishing Muhammad cartoons. Attack shocked France and world, viewed as attack on freedom of speech. Millions marched in Paris and nationwide, holding 'Je suis Charlie' signs, defending freedom of speech. But attack also intensified debates about freedom of speech limits, religious offense and Muslim integration. Charlie Hebdo attack symbolized terrorism threat France faces, triggering intense discussions about secularism, identity and security.

events.title: Paris Terror Attacks
events.description: Islamic State terrorists launched coordinated attacks at multiple Paris locations including Bataclan theater, Stade de France and restaurants, killing 130, injuring hundreds. This was France's worst attack since WWII. President Hollande declared state of emergency, France intensified counter-terrorism operations, bombed Islamic State targets in Syria. Attacks triggered debates about security, immigration, radicalization, strengthening far-right. Paris attacks became symbol of global war on terror, also exposed Europe's vulnerability. France united, but social tensions and divisions intensified.

events.title: Macron Elected President
events.description: 39-year-old Emmanuel Macron with newly formed 'En Marche' movement defeated far-right Marine Le Pen, elected president, becoming France's youngest president. Macron centrist, neither traditional left nor right, promised reform and modernization. His victory shattered traditional party system, Socialist and Republican parties collapsed. Macron pushed labor law reform, pension reform, supported European integration, but faced strong opposition like Yellow Vest movement. Macron represented French politics' reorganization, but also exposed elite-populace divide.

events.title: Yellow Vest Movement
events.description: Populace protested fuel tax increase, evolved into massive social movement, demonstrating every Saturday nationwide. Protesters wore yellow reflective vests (French drivers' requirement), demanded lower living costs, tax justice, more democracy. Movement leaderless, unorganized, mobilized through social media. Demonstrations often turned violent, Champs-Élysées vandalized, Arc de Triomphe graffitied. Macron forced to cancel fuel tax, increase minimum wage, hold national debate. Yellow Vest movement reflected provinces', working class' anger at elites, globalization, inequality, manifestation of France's deep social divisions.

events.title: Notre-Dame Fire
events.description: Notre-Dame de Paris caught fire, iconic spire collapsed, roof destroyed. World watched in shock as this 850-year-old Gothic masterpiece burned. Firefighters battled for hours, saved main structure and most artifacts. Fire cause possibly restoration work accident. President Macron pledged to rebuild Notre-Dame within five years, launched international fundraising. Notre-Dame fire touched French emotions, symbolizing cultural heritage's fragility and national identity. Reconstruction became national unity project, planned for completion before 2024 Paris Olympics.

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.description: COVID-19 pandemic struck France, causing tens of thousands of deaths, economic shutdown. Government implemented strict lockdowns, restricted movement, closed schools and businesses. Healthcare system overwhelmed, especially eastern regions. Pandemic exposed healthcare system weaknesses and social inequalities. Macron government launched massive economic support plan, protecting jobs and businesses. Vaccination campaign faced hesitancy and opposition, triggering health pass controversy. Pandemic intensified political divisions, trust in government declined. France with Europe jointly addressed crisis, but also exposed solidarity's limits.

events.title: Contemporary France
events.description: France is world's seventh-largest economy, UN Security Council permanent member, nuclear power, EU core member. Paris is global capital of culture, fashion and gastronomy. But France faces numerous challenges: slow economic growth, high unemployment (especially youth), heavy public debt, unsustainable pension system. Social divisions intensifying: urban vs rural, elite vs populace, immigration integration issues, Islamic extremism threat. Political polarization, far-right National Rally rising, traditional parties declining. Climate change, European integration's future, relations with US and China are key issues. Despite heavy challenges, France maintains its cultural influence and commitment to human rights, secularism, republican values. France's history is complex interweaving of revolution and reaction, glory and trauma, universal ideals and nationalism, these tensions continue shaping its present and future.
